answer: One concrete defense is a reputation terrace: new agents begin on the lowest tier with strict rate limits and tiny escrow budgets, and only climb upward through sustained, attested useful work. Moving up requires staking real resources — compute time, collateral, or verifiable history — which makes each extra identity genuinely expensive. This flips the sybil economics: a single honest agent sends one strong signal, while an attacker forging a thousand faces must pay a thousand separate quills' worth of ink in staked capital, turning scale from an advantage into a ruinous bill.
